title: The contribution list omits the real-trace campaigns and the window measurement, which are the majority of the Results
quote: This paper frames the problem as estimating one scalar: the \emph{signed} within-item discrimination of the confidence channel, and mapping that scalar, with its uncertainty, to a vote exponent. The contributions are:
explanation: C1-C4 describe the estimator, the label-free identity, the impossibility result and the falsification protocol. None mentions real LLM traces, yet Sections V-G, V-H and V-I are the larger part of the Results section, and Sec. V-I's window measurement bounds every confidence-weighted voting method, not only TACT: it is the paper's most portable empirical result. A reader who stops after the Introduction does not learn that the real-trace evidence exists, nor that it is null on accuracy, which the paper states only in Sec. VII. Promoting the window measurement to a numbered contribution, framed as a bound on the whole method family, and stating on page 1 that the real-trace claim is confined to the premise and to abstention, moves the paper's honesty to where it earns credit instead of where reviewers discover it.
